title: Security posture discovery with Elysium Systems
summary: Intro call to understand Elysium's security requirements for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule SE deep-dive for Dedicated/private network options, and provide retention/ingestion docs.
topics: SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC & least privilege, audit logging and log retention, encryption at rest/in transit (KMS, HSM options), data residency and retention policies, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, pilot/POC scope and timeline.
action_items: Maya Patel | Send SOC 2 Type II attestation, ISO 27001 cert, and security deck | due 2027-08-10
Ethan Cole | Prepare Dedicated/private architecture slide (VPC peering, private control plane) and list of supported KMS/HSM integrations | due 2027-08-12
Sara Lin | Share Elysium's data classification matrix and regulatory constraints (PCI/PHI notes) | due 2027-08-11
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security pack
Schedule SE deep dive (Dedicated + Private networking) for week of 2027-08-16
Customer to circulate internal data classification and target retention SLAs
Agree on pilot scope (10k inference calls/day, 30 day window)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sara (CISO - Elysium), Tom (Head of Platform), Priya (DevSecOps), Luis (SRE)

Summary: quick intros, high level security posture questions, technical clarifications on Dedicated vs Private network, encryption/KMS details, and next steps to share artifacts and schedule deep dive.

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, and with me is ethan our se. hows everyone doing?
[00:12] Sara Lin: good thanks, yeah we wanted to carve out time to go through security posture. Elysium's looking at three deployment options, hosted, dedicated, or a private deployment, so we need to understand the controls.
[00:25] Ethan Cole: great, we can walk through both the compliance attestations and the technical controls. quick question up front — are you looking for SOC two type two specifically or ISO as well?
[00:36] Tom Alvarez: primarily SOC2, but iso 27001 would be a bonus for our procurement team. also SSO is non-negotiable, we need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[00:47] Maya Patel: totally — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, i'll share those artifacts after the call. we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; our RBAC model maps to groups and roles — can do fine-grained access for routes and models.
[01:05] Priya Singh: when you say RBAC maps to groups, is that enforced at the control plane or do we get token-level restrictions per API key?
[01:15] Ethan Cole: good Q. RBAC and token scoping are in the control plane, you can issue scoped API keys for specific routes/models and set allowed actions. enforcement is at the gateway and at the runtime, so the token won't be able to call disallowed endpoints.
[01:30] Luis Moreno: how about audit logs — what gets logged and retention? we need immutable logs for 1 year minimum, pushed to our SIEM.
[01:40] Maya Patel: we keep detailed audit trails: auth events, model calls, admin actions, and config changes. logs can be exported to your S3/Syslog/CloudWatch and we support push to third-party SIEMs. retention default is 90 days on hosted, but Dedicated/Private options allow longer retention or forwarding for indefinite storage.
[01:59] Sara Lin: ok that sounds promising. encryption — is data encrypted at rest by default? and what KMS options do you support?
[02:09] Ethan Cole: yes, everything is encrypted in transit and at rest by default. For Hosted we use our managed KMS, but for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS; we support cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations for higher assurance. note: i sometimes say "Redwood Dedicate" — that's our fault, it's Dedicated.
[02:35] Tom Alvarez: do you have support for customer-managed keys plus HSM-backed signing? some of our compliance requires HSM attestations.
[02:44] Ethan Cole: yep, HSM-backed keys are supported in Private deployments; Dedicated can be configured to point to your KMS with customer-managed keys. we'll include details in the architecture doc.
[02:58] Priya Singh: data residency — can we ensure inference data doesn't leave eu-west? we have eu-only residency requirements for a subset of workloads.
[03:09] Maya Patel: absolutely — we can pin routing by region; Hosted has regional endpoints, Dedicated gives you regional capacity, and Private is fully in your VPC/region. for strict residency we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:24] Luis Moreno: curious about caching — you mentioned KV cache in your docs, does that persist any user data? we need to avoid persisting pii in caches.
[03:35] Ethan Cole: good catch — the KV cache is for model context only and can be configured to avoid persisting raw customer data. there are policies to scrub or not cache prefixes, and you can disable prefix caching entirely for sensitive workloads.
[03:51] Sara Lin: what about integration with our SSO and SCIM? we use okta and azure ad.
[03:58] Maya Patel: we have out-of-the-box SAML integrations with Okta and AAD, SCIM provisioning for groups and users, and support SSO session policies. i'll send the SSO configuration guide.
[04:12] Tom Alvarez: how do you handle incident response and breach notifications? our policy requires 72-hour notif and a runbook.
[04:21] Ethan Cole: we have a documented incident response process, notify customers per contract timelines (72 hours standard for incidents with customer data). we also publish post-incident reports to affected customers and have SOC 2 controls around monitoring. will share our IR runbook excerpt.
[04:38] Priya Singh: curious about network isolation for Dedicated — do we get private control plane or just private data plane?
[04:46] Ethan Cole: for Dedicated we offer customer-dedicated GPU pools and private networking; the control plane can be configured to be private via VPC peering or a private endpoint. for the most stringent cases we recommend Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed.
[05:02] Maya Patel: i'll be clear in the follow-up doc: Hosted = fastest, but managed keys and standard retention; Dedicated = reserved capacity, VPC options, BYOK; Private = fully on-prem or VPC with private control plane and HSM options.
[05:18] Luis Moreno: any regulatory attestations beyond SOC2/ISO? we have some PCI-scope services.
[05:24] Maya Patel: we can share a compliance matrix; for PCI or PHI workloads we typically advise Private deployments or strict Dedicated contracts with contractual commitments.
[05:33] Sara Lin: on the topic of logs and monitoring, can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns? that's important for our chargeback.
[05:42] Ethan Cole: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost/latency, per-model dashboards, and traces. for Dedicated/Private we can forward metrics to your monitoring stack and enable low-level traces.
[05:55] Tom Alvarez: what's the typical SLA for Dedicated? we need uptime and latency SLOs.
[06:01] Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include sample SLAs and the service credits model in the follow-up.
[06:10] Priya Singh: any tenant isolation guarantees? how do you prevent cross-tenant data leakage?
[06:16] Ethan Cole: multi-tenancy is strictly isolated at runtime; cryptographic separation of keys and per-tenant models. for extra assurance Private gives you single-tenant control.
[06:29] Sara Lin: ok, makes sense. what about logging schema and whether logs contain PII? we need to know which fields are logged so we can map to our DLP.
[06:41] Maya Patel: logs capture request metadata, timestamps, model IDs, token counts, and anonymized request IDs by default. payloads are not stored in plain text unless you enable full request logging for debugging; we recommend redaction and sample logging for sensitive workloads.
[07:02] Luis Moreno: would you allow us to ship logs directly to our S3 with server-side encryption?
[07:09] Ethan Cole: yes, we support direct log export to S3 with SSE, and you can configure the bucket to use your KMS keys.
[07:18] Tom Alvarez: procurement will want lead times — if we pick Dedicated, how long to provision?
[07:24] Maya Patel: Dedicated provisioning is usually a few days to a couple of weeks depending on capacity and region; Private/on-prem is longer (weeks-months) because of on-site setup. we'll add timeline estimates in the follow-up.
[07:38] Priya Singh: for the pilot, we want to validate that keys never leave our control. is there a handshake or attestation?
[07:45] Ethan Cole: for BYOK we do key wrapping and HSM attestations where supported; we'll provide the integration guide and example key policies.
[07:56] Sara Lin: any open questions from your side?
[08:00] Maya Patel: just want to confirm retention target — you mentioned 1 year for audit logs; do you want inference logs retained too?
[08:07] Sara Lin: inference logs aggregated and anonymized for 90 days is fine, but audit/admin logs should be one year.
[08:14] Maya Patel: got it. we'll propose a configuration in the doc: inference 90d, audit 365d, and option to forward to your S3 for indefinite retention.
[08:25] Tom Alvarez: can you also include pricing delta for longer retention and BYOK?
[08:30] Maya Patel: yes we'll include a Dedicated pricing appendix and the Dedicated vs Private cost considerations.
[08:36] Luis Moreno: last thing — do you run third-party pen tests or do you provide pentest reports?
[08:41] Ethan Cole: we have third-party security assessments and can share summary reports under NDA; for Private deployments we can coordinate scoping if you want a joint test.
[08:52] Priya Singh: cool, thanks.
[08:55] Maya Patel: thanks all. we'll follow up with the SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO guide, Dedicated architecture, and schedule the SE deep-dive.
[09:03] Sara Lin: thanks everybody. looking forward to the docs.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor mishearings (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated"). Links shared: security pack (link to redwood security pack) — will be attached in CRM and email.
